All environment variables are available by referencing [`env.Env`](../functions/env/#envenv) 9 (or [`env.Getenv`](../functions/env/#envgetenv)) in the template. 10 11 The template is read from standard in, and written to standard out. 12 13 Use it like this: 14 15 ```console 16 $ echo "Hello, {{ env.Env.USER }}" | gomplate 17 Hello, hairyhenderson 18 ``` 19 20 ## Commandline Arguments 21 22 ### `--config` 23 24 Specify the path to a [gomplate config file](../config). The default is `.gomplate.yaml`. Can also be set with the `GOMPLATE_CONFIG` environment variable. Setting `--config` or `GOMPLATE_CONFIG` to an empty string (`--config=""` or `export GOMPLATE_CONFIG=""`) will disable the use of a config file, skipping the default `.gomplate.yaml` file. 25 26 For example: 27 28 ```console 29 $ cat myconfig.yaml 30 in: hello {{ .data.thing }} 31 32 datasources: 33 data: 34 url: https://example.com/data.json 35 $ gomplate --config myconfig.yaml 36 hello world 37 ``` 38 39 ### `--file`/`-f`, `--in`/`-i`, and `--out`/`-o` 40 41 By default, `gomplate` will read from `Stdin` and write to `Stdout`. This behaviour can be changed. 42 43 - Use `--file`/`-f` to use a specific input template file. The special value `-` means `Stdin`. 44 - Use `--out`/`-o` to save output to file. The special value `-` means `Stdout`. 45 - Use `--in`/`-i` if you want to set the input template right on the commandline. This overrides `--file`. Because of shell command line lengths, it's probably not a good idea to use a very long value with this argument. 46 47 #### Multiple inputs 48 49 You can specify multiple `--file` and `--out` arguments. The same number of each much be given. This allows `gomplate` to process multiple templates _slightly_ faster than invoking `gomplate` multiple times in a row. 50 51 ### `--input-dir` and `--output-dir` 52 53 For processing multiple templates in a directory you can use `--input-dir` and `--output-dir` together. In this case all files in input directory will be processed recursively as templates and the resulting files stored in `--output-dir`. The output directory will be created if it does not exist and the directory structure of the input directory will be preserved. 54 55 You can use the [`--exclude`](#--exclude-and---include) argument and/or a [`.gomplateignore`](#gomplateignore-files) file to exclude some of the files in the input directory. 56 57 Example: 58 59 ```bash 60 # Process all files in directory "templates" with the datasource given 61 # and store the files with the same directory structure in "config" 62 gomplate --input-dir=templates --output-dir=config --datasource config=config.yaml 63 ``` 64 65 ### `--output-map` 66 67 Sometimes a 1-to-1 mapping between input filenames and output filenames is not desirable. For these cases, you can supply a template string as the argument to `--output-map`. The template string is interpreted as a regular gomplate template, and all datasources and external nested templates are available to the output map template. 68 69 A new [context][] is provided, with the input filename is available at `.in`, and the original context is available at `.ctx`. For convenience, any context keys not conflicting with `in` or `ctx` are also copied. 70 71 All whitespace on the left or right sides of the output is trimmed. 72 73 For example, given an input directory `in/` containing files with the extension `.yaml.tmpl`, if we want to rename those to `.yaml`: 74 75 ```console 76 $ gomplate --input-dir=in/ --output-map='out/{{ .in | strings.ReplaceAll ".yaml.tmpl" ".yaml" }}' 77 ``` 78 79 #### Referencing complex output map template files 80 81 It may be useful to store more complex output map templates in a file. This can be done with [external templates][]. 82 83 Consider a template `out.t`: 84 85 ``` 86 {{- /* .in may contain a directory name - we want to preserve that */ -}} 87 {{ $f := filepath.Base .in -}} 88 out/{{ .in | strings.ReplaceAll $f (index .filemap $f) }}.out 89 ``` 90 91 And a datasource `filemap.json`: 92 93 ```json 94 { "eins.txt": "uno", "deux.txt": "dos" } 95 ``` 96 97 We can blend these two together: 98 99 ```console 100 $ gomplate -t out=out.t -c filemap.json --input-dir=in --output-map='{{ template "out" . }}' 101 ``` 102 103 ### `--chmod` 104 105 By default, output files are created with the same file mode (permissions) as input files. If desired, the `--chmod` option can be used to override this behaviour, and set the output file mode explicitly. This can be useful for creating executable scripts or ensuring write permissions. 106 107 The value must be an octal integer in the standard UNIX `chmod` format, i.e. `644` to indicate that owner gets read+write, group gets read-only, and others get read-only permissions. See the [`chmod(1)` man page](https://linux.die.net/man/1/chmod) for more details. 108 109 **Note:** `--chmod` is supported on Windows, but only read/write (`666`) and read-only (`444`). If you pass a value like `755` on Windows, gomplate will reinterpret that as what you probably intended (read-write). 110 111 ### `--exclude` and `--include` 112 113 When using the [`--input-dir`](#--input-dir-and---output-dir) argument, it can be useful to filter which files are processed. You can use `--exclude` and `--include` to achieve this. The `--exclude` flag takes a [`.gitignore`][]-style pattern, and any files matching the pattern will be excluded. The `--include` flag is effectively the opposite of `--exclude`. You can also repeat the arguments to provide a series of patterns to be excluded/included. 114 115 Patterns provided with `--exclude`/`--include` are matched relative to the input directory. 116 117 _Note:_ These patterns are _not_ treated as filesystem globs, and so a pattern like `/foo/bar.json` will match relative to the input directory, not the root of the filesystem as they may appear! 118 119 Examples: 120 121 ```console 122 $ gomplate --exclude example/** --exclude *.png --input-dir in/ --output-dir out/ 123 ``` 124 125 This will stop all files in the `in/example` directory from being processed, as well as all `.png` files in the `in/` directory. 126 127 ```console 128 $ gomplate --include *.tmpl --exclude foo*.tmpl --input-dir in/ --output-dir out/ 129 ``` 130 131 This will cause only files ending in `.tmpl` to be processed, except for files with names beginning with `foo`: `template.tmpl` will be included, but `foo-template.tmpl` will not. 132 133 ### `--exclude-processing` 134 135 When using the [`--input-dir`](#--input-dir-and---output-dir) argument, it can be useful to skip some files from processing and copy them directly to the output directory. Like the `--exclude` flag, it takes a [`.gitignore`][]-style pattern, and any files match the pattern will be copied. 136 137 _Note:_ These patterns are _not_ treated as filesystem globs, and so a pattern like `/foo/bar.json` will match relative to the input directory, not the root of the filesystem as they may appear! 138 139 Examples: 140 141 ```console 142 $ gomplate --exclude-processing '*.png' --input-dir in/ --output-dir out/ 143 ``` 144 145 This will skip all `*.png` files in the `in/` directory from being processed, and copy them to the `out/` directory. 146 147 #### `.gomplateignore` files 148 149 You can also use a file named `.gomplateignore` containing one exclude pattern on each line. This has the same syntax as a [`.gitignore`][] file. 150 When processing sub-directories, `.gomplateignore` files in the parent directory are also considered. Patterns are matched relative to the location of the `.gomplateignore` file. 151 152 ### `--datasource`/`-d` 153 154 Add a data source in `name=URL` form. Specify multiple times to add multiple sources. The data can then be used by the [`datasource`](../functions/data/#datasource) and [`include`](../functions/data/#include) functions. 155 156 Data sources referenced in this way are lazy-loaded: they will not be read until the template is parsed and a `datasource` or `include` function is encountered. 157 158 See [Datasources](../datasources) for full details. 159 160 A few different forms are valid: 161 162 - `mydata=file:///tmp/my/file.json` 163 - Create a data source named `mydata` which is read from `/tmp/my/file.json`. This form is valid for any file in any path. 164 - `mydata=file.json` 165 - Create a data source named `mydata` which is read from `file.json` (in the current working directory). This form is only valid for files in the current directory. 166 - `mydata.json` 167 - This form infers the name from the file name (without extension). Only valid for files in the current directory. 168 169 170 ### `--datasource-header`/`-H` 171 172 Provides one (or more) HTTP headers to be sent along with the matching 173 HTTP-based datasource. Value is in the form `alias="HeaderName: header-value"`. 174 175 Note that the `alias` does not need to map to a datasource specified in a 176 command-line flag, but can be used in dynamically-defined datasources (see 177 [`defineDatasource`](../functions/data#definedatasource)). 178 179 ### `--context`/`-c` 180 181 Add a data source in `name=URL` form, and make it available in the [default context][] as `.`. The special name `.` (period) can be used to override the entire default context. 182 183 Data sources referenced with `--context` will be immediately loaded before gomplate processes the template. This is in contrast to the `--datasource` behaviour, which lazy-loads data while processing the template. 184 185 All other rules for the [`--datasource`/`-d`](#--datasource-d) flag apply. 186 187 Examples: 188 189 ```console 190 $ gomplate --context post=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/2 -i 'post title is: {{ .post.title }}' 191 post title is: qui est esse 192 ``` 193 194 ```console 195 $ gomplate -c .=http://xkcd.com/info.0.json -i '{{ .title }}' 196 Diploma Legal Notes 197 ``` 198 199 ### `--missing-key` 200 201 Control the behavior during execution if a map is indexed with a key that is not present in the map. 202 203 Available values: 204 - `error` (default): Execution stops immediately with an error. 205 - `default` or `invalid`: Do nothing and continue execution. If printed, the result is the string `""`. 206 - `zero`: The operation returns the zero value for the element (which may be `nil`, in which case the string `""` is printed). 207 208 Examples: 209 210 ```console 211 $ gomplate --missing-key error -i 'Hi {{ .name }}' 212 Hi 14:06:57 ERR error="failed to render template : template: :1:6: executing \"\" at <.name>: map has no entry for key \"name\"" 213 ``` 214 215 ```console 216 $ gomplate --missing-key default -i 'Hi {{ .name }}' 217 Hi 218 ``` 219 220 ```console 221 $ gomplate --missing-key zero -i 'Hi {{ .name | default "Alex" }}' 222 Hi Alex 223 ``` 224 225 ```console 226 $ gomplate --missing-key zero -i 'Hi {{ .name | required }}' 227 Hi 14:12:04 ERR error="failed to render template : template: :1:11: executing \"\" at : error calling required: can not render template: a required value was not set" 228 ``` 229 230 231 ### Overriding the template delimiters 232 233 Sometimes it's necessary to override the default template delimiters (`{{`/`}}`). 234 Use `--left-delim`/`--right-delim` or set `$GOMPLATE_LEFT_DELIM`/`$GOMPLATE_RIGHT_DELIM`. 235 236 ### `--template`/`-t` 237 238 Add a nested template or directory of templates that can be referenced by the 239 main input template(s) with the [`template`](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template/#hdr-Actions) 240 built-in or the functions in the [`tmpl`](../functions/tmpl/) namespace. Specify 241 multiple times to add multiple template references. 242 243 Similar to data sources, the value is a `alias=url` pair, where `alias` is the 244 template name and `url` is an optionally-relative URL to the template file or 245 directory. Note that currently only `file:` URLs are supported. 246 247 In addition to the `alias=url` form, in certain cases the alias may be omitted, 248 in which case the `url` will be used as the `alias`. When referencing a 249 directory, all files in the directory will be included, available to be 250 referenced as `alias/`. 251 252 Some examples: 253 254 - `--template foo=file:///tmp/foo.tmpl` 255 - References a file `/tmp/foo.tmpl` 256 - It will be available as a template named `foo`: 257 258 ```console 259 $ gomplate --template foo=file:///tmp/foo.tmpl -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "foo" }} ]' 260 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 261 ``` 262 - `--template mytemplate.t` 263 - References a file `mytemplate.t` in the current working directory. 264 - It will be available as a template named `mytemplate.t`: 265 266 ```console 267 $ gomplate --template helloworld.tmpl -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "helloworld.tmpl" }} ]' 268 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 269 ``` 270 - `--template path/to/mytemplate.t` 271 - References a file `mytemplate.t` in the path `path/to/`. 272 - It will be available as a template named `path/to/mytemplate.t`: 273 274 ```console 275 $ gomplate --template foo/bar/helloworld.tmpl -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "foo/bar/helloworld.tmpl" }} ]' 276 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 277 ``` 278 - `--template path/to/` 279 - Makes available all files in the path `path/to/`. 280 - Any files within this path can be referenced: 281 282 ```console 283 $ gomplate --template foo/bar/ -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "foo/bar/helloworld.tmpl" }} ]' 284 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 285 ``` 286 - `--template alias=path/to/mytemplate.t` 287 - References a file `mytemplate.t` in the path `path/to/` 288 - It will be available as a template named `alias`: 289 290 ```console 291 $ gomplate --template t=foo/bar/helloworld.tmpl -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "t" }} ]' 292 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 293 ``` 294 - `--template alias=path/to/` 295 - Makes available all files in the path `path/to/`. 296 - Any files within this path can be referenced, with the path replaced with `alias`: 297 298 ```console 299 $ gomplate --template dir=foo/bar/ -i 'here are the contents of the template: [ {{ template "dir/helloworld.tmpl" }} ]' 300 here are the contents of the template: [ hello, world! ] 301 ``` 302 303 ### `--plugin` 304 305 _See the [config file](../config/#plugins) for more plugin configuration options._ 306 307 Some specialized use cases may need functionality that gomplate isn't capable 308 of on its own. If you have a command or script to perform this functionality, 309 you can plug in your own custom functions with the `--plugin` flag: 310 311 ```console 312 $ gomplate --plugin echo=/bin/echo -i 'Hello {{ echo "World" }}' 313 Hello World 314 ``` 315 316 All arguments provided to the function will be passed as positional arguments to 317 the plugin, and the plugin's standard output stream (`Stdout`) will be printed 318 to the rendered output. To instead pipe the final argument of the function to 319 the plugin's standard input stream, use the [config file](../config/#plugins) 320 and set the `pipe` field. 321 322 If the plugin exits with a non-zero exit code, gomplate will also fail. All signals 323 caught by gomplate will be propagated to the plugin. Any output on the standard 324 error stream will be printed to gomplate's standard error stream. 325 326 Plugins can also be written as PowerShell or CMD scripts (`.ps1`, `.bat`, or `.cmd` 327 extensions) on Windows. 328 329 By default, plugins will time out after 5 seconds. To adjust this, set the 330 `GOMPLATE_PLUGIN_TIMEOUT` environment variable to a valid [duration](../functions/time/#timeparseduration) 331 such as `10s` or `3m`, or use the [`pluginTimeout`](../config/#plugintimeout) 332 configuration option. 333 334 ### `--exec-pipe` 335 336 When using [post-template command execution](#post-template-command-execution), 337 it may be useful to pipe gomplate's rendered output directly into the command's 338 standard input. 339 340 To do this, simply use `--exec-pipe` instead of `--out` or any other output flag: 341 342 ```console 343 $ gomplate -i 'hello world' --exec-pipe -- tr a-z A-Z 344 HELLO WORLD 345 ``` 346 347 Note that multiple inputs are not yet supported when using this option. 348 349 ### `--experimental` 350 351 Use this flag to enable experimental functionality. See the docs for the 352 [`experimental`](../config/#experimental) configuration option for more 353 information. 354 355 ### `--verbose` 356 357 When you specify `--verbose`, gomplate will log some extra information useful 358 for debugging and troubleshooting. 359 360 All log output is done on the _standard error_ stream, and so will never 361 interrupt rendered output. For example, redirecting output to a file or another 362 command will work as expected, without the log output interfering. 363 364 ## Log formatting 365 366 The `GOMPLATE_LOG_FORMAT` environment variable can be used to control the format 367 of the log messages that gomplate may output, whether error messages or debug 368 messages when the [`--verbose`](#--verbose) option is in use. 369 370 The value can be set to `json` or `logfmt`. 371 372 #### `json` format 373 374 `json` is the default format when gomplate is used in a script or non-interactive 375 terminal. 376 377 ```console 378 $ GOMPLATE_LOG_FORMAT=json gomplate -i '{{' 379 380 {"level":"error","error":"template: :1: unexpected unclosed action in command","time":"2021-01-24T20:49:02-05:00"} 381 ``` 382 383 #### `console` format 384 385 `console` is the default format used when gomplate is used in an interactive terminal. 386 Messages are printed in colour when possible. 387 388 ```console 389 $ GOMPLATE_LOG_FORMAT=console gomplate -i '{{' 390 391 20:49:28 ERR error="template: :1: unexpected unclosed action in command" 392 ``` 393 394 #### `logfmt` format 395 396 `logfmt` format is a simple structured `key=value` format. 397 398 ```console 399 $ GOMPLATE_LOG_FORMAT=logfmt bin/gomplate -i '{{' 400 401 time=2021-01-24T20:50:58-05:00 level=error error="template: :1: unexpected unclosed action in command" 402 ``` 403 404 #### `simple` format 405 406 `simple` omits the level and timestamp for a very simplistic output. 407 408 ```console 409 $ GOMPLATE_LOG_FORMAT=simple bin/gomplate -i '{{' 410 411 error="template: :1: unexpected unclosed action in command" 412 ``` 413 414 ## Post-template command execution 415 416 Gomplate can launch other commands when template execution is successful. Simply 417 add the command to the command-line after a `--` argument: 418 419 ```console 420 $ gomplate -i 'hello world' -o out.txt -- cat out.txt 421 hello world 422 ``` 423 424 See also [`--exec-pipe`](#--exec-pipe) for piping output directly into the 425 post-exec command. 426 427 ## Empty output 428 429 If the template renders to an empty file (i.e. output consisting of only whitespace), gomplate will not write the output. 430 431 432 [default context]: ../syntax/#the-context 433 [context]: ../syntax/#the-context 434 [external templates]: ../syntax/#external-templates 435 [`.gitignore`]: https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore

1	---
2	title: Datasources
3	weight: 14
4	menu: main
5	---
6	
7	Datasources are an optional, but central concept in gomplate. While the basic flow of template rendering is taking an input template and rendering it into an output, there often is need to include data from one or more sources external to the template itself.
8	
9	Some common use-cases include injecting sensitive material like passwords (which should not be stored unencrypted in source-control with the templates), or providing simplified configuration formats that can be fed to a template to provide a much more complex output.
10	
11	Datasources can be defined with the [`--datasource`/`-d`][] command-line flag or the [`defineDatasource`][] function, and referenced via an _alias_ inside the template, using a function such as [`datasource`][] or [`include`][]. Datasources can additionally be loaded into the [context][] with the [`--context`/`-c`][] command-line flag.
12	
13	Since datasources are defined separately from the template, the same templates can be used with different datasources and even different datasource types. For example, gomplate could be run on a developer machine with a `file` datasource pointing to a JSON file containing test data, where the same template could be used in a production environment using a `consul` datasource with the real production data.
14	
15	## URL Format
16	
17	All datasources are defined with a [URL][]. As a refresher, a URL is made up of the following components:
18	
19	```pre
20	  foo://userinfo@example.com:8042/over/there?name=ferret#nose
21	  \_/   \_______________________/\_________/ \_________/ \__/
22	   |           |                    |            |        |
23	scheme     authority               path        query   fragment
24	```
25	
26	For our purposes, the _scheme_ and the _path_ components are especially important, though the other components are used by certain datasources for particular purposes.
27	
28	| component | purpose |
29	|-----------|---------|
30	| _scheme_ | Identifies which [datasource](#supported-datasources) to access. All datasources require a scheme (except for `file` when using relative paths), and some datasources allow multiple different schemes to clarify access modes, such as `consul+https` |
31	| _authority_ | Used only by remote datasources, and can be omitted in some of those cases. Consists of _userinfo_ (`user:pass`), _host_, and _port_. |
32	| _path_ | Can be omitted, but usually used as the basis of the locator for the datasource. If the path ends with a `/` character, [directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are used. |
33	| _query_ | Used rarely for datasources where information must be provided in order to get a reasonable reply (such as generating dynamic secrets with Vault), or for [overriding MIME types](#overriding-mime-types) |
34	| _fragment_ | Used rarely for accessing a subset of the given path |
35	
36	### Opaque URIs
37	
38	For some datasources, such as the [`merge`](#using-merge-datasources), [`aws+sm`](#using-awssm-datasources), and [`aws+smp`](#using-awssmp-datasources) schemes, opaque URIs can be used (rather than a hierarchical URL):
39	
40	```pre
41	scheme                   path        query   fragment
42	   |   _____________________|__   _______|_   _|
43	  / \ /                        \ /         \ /  \
44	  urn:example:animal:ferret:nose?name=ferret#nose
45	```
46	
47	The semantics of the different URI components are essentially the same as for hierarchical URLs (see above),
48	but the _path_ component may not start with a `/` character. In gomplate's usage, opaque URIs sometimes contain
49	characters such as `|`, which require escaping with most shells. You may need to surround the datasource definition
50	in quotes, or use the `\` escape character.
51	
52	## Supported datasources
53	
54	Gomplate supports a number of datasources, each specified with a particular URL scheme. The table below describes these datasources. The names in the _Type_ column link to further documentation for each specific datasource.
55	
56	| Type | URL Scheme(s) | Description |
57	|------|---------------|-------------|
58	| [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](#using-awssmp-datasources) | `aws+smp` | [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store][AWS SMP] is a hierarchically-organized key/value store which allows storage of text, lists, or encrypted secrets for retrieval by AWS resources |
59	| [AWS Secrets Manager](#using-awssm-datasources) | `aws+sm` | [AWS Secrets Manager][] helps you protect secrets needed to access your applications, services, and IT resources. |
60	| [Amazon S3](#using-s3-datasources) | `s3` | [Amazon S3][] is a popular object storage service. |
61	| [Consul](#using-consul-datasources) | `consul`, `consul+http`, `consul+https` | [HashiCorp Consul][] provides (among many other features) a key/value store |
62	| [Environment](#using-env-datasources) | `env` | Environment variables can be used as datasources - useful for testing |
63	| [File](#using-file-datasources) | `file` | Files can be read in any of the [supported formats](#mime-types), including by piping through standard input (`Stdin`). [Directories](#directory-datasources) are also supported. |
64	| [Git](#using-git-datasources) | `git`, `git+file`, `git+http`, `git+https`, `git+ssh` | Files can be read from a local or remote git repository, at specific branches or tags. [Directory semantics](#directory-datasources) are also supported. |
65	| [GCP Compute Instance Metadata](#using-gcpmeta-datasources) | `gcp+meta` | Provides access to the [GCP VM Metadata Service][], including instance and project metadata. |
66	| [Google Cloud Storage](#using-google-cloud-storage-gs-datasources) | `gs` | [Google Cloud Storage][] is the object storage service available on GCP, comparable to AWS S3. |
67	| [HTTP](#using-http-datasources) | `http`, `https` | Data can be sourced from HTTP/HTTPS sites in many different formats. Arbitrary HTTP headers can be set with the [`--datasource-header`/`-H`][] flag |
68	| [Merged Datasources](#using-merge-datasources) | `merge` | Merge two or more datasources together to produce the final value - useful for resolving defaults. Uses [`coll.Merge`][] for merging. |
69	| [Stdin](#using-stdin-datasources) | `stdin` | A special case of the `file` datasource; allows piping through standard input (`Stdin`) |
70	| [Vault](#using-vault-datasources) | `vault`, `vault+http`, `vault+https` | [HashiCorp Vault][] is an industry-leading open-source secret management tool. [List support](#directory-datasources) is also available. |
71	
72	## Directory Datasources
73	
74	When the _path_ component of the URL ends with a `/` character, the datasource is read with _directory_ semantics. Not all datasource types support this, and for those that don't support the notion of a directory, the behaviour is currently undefined. See each documentation section for details.
75	 
76	Currently the following datasources support directory semantics:
77	
78	- [File](#using-file-datasources)
79	- [Vault](#using-vault-datasources) - translates to Vault's `LIST` method
80	- [Consul](#using-consul-datasources)
81	When accessing a directory datasource, an array of key names is returned, and can be iterated through to access each individual value contained within.
82	- [AWS S3](#using-s3-datasources)
83	- [Google Cloud Storage](#using-google-cloud-storage-gs-datasources)
84	- [Git](#using-git-datasources) 
85	- [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](#using-awssmp-datasources)
86	
87	For example, a group of configuration key/value pairs (named `one`, `two`, and `three`, with values `v1`, `v2`, and `v3` respectively) could be rendered like this: 
88	
89	_template.tmpl:_
90	```
91	{{ range (datasource "config") -}}
92	{{ . }} = {{ (datasource "config" .).value }}
93	{{- end }}
94	```
95	
96	```console
97	$ gomplate -d config=vault:///secret/configs/ -f template.tmpl
98	one = v1
99	two = v2
100	three = v3
101	```
102	
103	## MIME Types
104	
105	Gomplate will read and parse a number of data formats. The appropriate type will be set automatically, if possible, either based on file extension (for the `file`, `http`, `gs`, and `s3` datasources), or the [HTTP Content-Type][] header, if available. If an unsupported type is detected, gomplate will exit with an error.
106	
107	These are the supported types:
108	
109	| Format | MIME Type | Extension(s) | Notes |
110	|--------|-----------|-------|------|
111	| CSV | `text/csv` | `.csv` | Uses the [`data.CSV`][] function to present the file as a 2-dimensional row-first string array |
112	| JSON | `application/json` | `.json` | [JSON][] _objects_ are assumed, but will support arrays as well. Other values are not parsed with this type. Uses the [`data.JSON`][] function for parsing. [EJSON][] (encrypted JSON) is supported and will be decrypted. |
113	| JSON Array | `application/array+json` | | A special type for parsing datasources containing just JSON arrays. Uses the [`data.JSONArray`][] function for parsing |
114	| Plain Text | `text/plain` | | Unstructured, and as such only intended for use with the [`include`][] function |
115	| TOML | `application/toml` | `.toml` | Parses [TOML][] with the [`data.TOML`][] function |
116	| YAML | `application/yaml` | `.yml`, `.yaml` | Parses [YAML][] with the [`data.YAML`][] function |
117	| [.env](#the-env-file-format) | `application/x-env` | `.env` | Basically just a file of `key=value` pairs separated by newlines, usually intended for sourcing into a shell. Common in [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/env-file/), [Ruby](https://github.com/bkeepers/dotenv), and [Node.js](https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv) applications. See [below](#the-env-file-format) for more information. |
118	
119	### Overriding MIME Types
120	
121	On occasion it's necessary to override the detected (via file extension or `Content-Type` header) MIME type. To accomplish this, gomplate supports a `type` query string parameter on datasource URLs. This can contain the same value as a standard [HTTP Content-Type][] header.
122	
123	For example, to force a file named `data.txt` to be parsed as a JSON document:
124	
125	```console
126	$ echo '{"foo": "bar"}' > /tmp/data.txt
127	$ gomplate -d data=file:///tmp/data.txt?type=application/json -i '{{ (ds "data").foo }}'
128	bar
129	```
130	
131	If you need to provide a query parameter named `type` to the data source, set the `GOMPLATE_TYPE_PARAM` environment variable to another value:
132	
133	```console
134	$ GOMPLATE_TYPE_PARAM=content-type gomplate -d data=https://example.com/mydata?content-type=application/json -i '{{ (ds "data").foo }}'
135	bar
136	```
137	
138	### The `.env` file format
139	
140	Many applications and frameworks support the use of a ".env" file for providing environment variables. It can also be considered a simple key/value file format, and as such can be used as a datasource in gomplate.
141	
142	To [override](#overriding-mime-types), use the unregistered `application/x-env` MIME type.
143	
144	Here's a sample explaining the syntax:
145	
146	```bash
147	FOO=a regular unquoted value
148	export BAR=another value, exports are ignored
149	
150	# comments are totally ignored, as are blank lines
151	FOO.BAR = "values can be double-quoted, and\tshell\nescapes are supported"
152	
153	BAZ="variable expansion: ${FOO}"
154	QUX='single quotes ignore $variables and newlines'
155	```
156	
157	The [`github.com/joho/godotenv`](https://github.com/joho/godotenv) package is used for parsing - see the full details there.
158	
159	
160	## Using `aws+smp` datasources
161	
162	The `aws+smp://` scheme can be used to retrieve data from the [AWS Systems Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/) (née AWS EC2 Simple Systems Manager) [Parameter Store][AWS SMP]. This hierarchically organized key/value store allows you to store text, lists or encrypted secrets for easy retrieval by AWS resources. See [the AWS Systems Manager documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-paramstore-su-create.html#sysman-paramstore-su-create-about) for details on creating these parameters.
163	
164	You must grant `gomplate` permission via IAM credentials for the [`ssm:GetParameter` action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-permissions-reference.html). <!-- List support further requires `ssm.GetParameters` permissions. -->
165	
166	See details on how to configure gomplate's AWS support in [_Configuring AWS_](../functions/aws/#configuring-aws).
167	
168	### URL Considerations
169	
170	The _scheme_ and _path_ URL components are used by this datasource. This may be an _opaque_ URI instead of an URL, when the key does not begin with a `/` character (e.g. `aws+smp:myparam`).
171	
172	- the _scheme_ must be `aws+smp`
173	- the _path_ component is used to specify the path to the parameter (this may be a hierarchical path beginning with `/`, or an opaque path). [Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
174	
175	### Output
176	
177	The output will be a single `Parameter` object from the
178	[AWS SDK for Go](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/ssm/#Parameter):
179	
180	| name   | description |
181	|--------|-------|
182	| `Name` | full Parameter name |
183	| `Type` | `String`, `StringList` or `SecureString` |
184	| `Value` | textual value, comma-separated single string if StringList |
185	| `Version` | incrementing integer version |
186	
187	If the Parameter key specified is not found (or not allowed to be read due to missing permissions) an error will be generated. There is no default.
188	
189	### Examples
190	
191	Given your AWS account's Parameter Store has the following data:
192	
193	- `/foo/first/others` - `Bill,Ben` (a StringList)
194	- `/foo/first/password` - `super-secret` (a SecureString)
195	- `/foo/second/p1` - `aaa`
196	- `myparameter` - `bar`
197	
198	```console
199	$ echo '{{ ds "foo" }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:///foo/first/password
200	map[Name:/foo/first/password Type:SecureString Value:super-secret Version:1]
201	
202	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo").Value }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:///foo/first/password
203	super-secret
204	
205	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo" "/foo/first/others").Value }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:
206	Bill,Ben
207	
208	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo" "/second/p1").Value }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:///foo/
209	aaa
210	
211	$ gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:///foo/first/ -i '{{ range (ds "foo") }}
212	{{ . }}: {{ (ds "foo" .).Value }}
213	{{- end }}'
214	others: Bill,Ben
215	password: super-secret
216	
217	$ gomplate -d foo=aws+smp:myparameter -i '{{ (ds "foo").Value }}
218	bar
219	```
220	
221	## Using `aws+sm` datasources
222	
223	### URL Considerations
224	
225	For `aws+sm`, only the _scheme_ and _path_ components are necessary to be defined. This may be an _opaque_ URI instead of an URL, when the key does not begin with a `/` character (e.g. `aws+sm:myparam`).
226	
227	- the _scheme_ must be `aws+sm`
228	- the _path_ component is used to specify the path to the secret (this may be a hierarchical path beginning with `/`, or an opaque path)
229	
230	### Output
231	
232	The output will be the content of either the `SecretString` or `SecretBinary` field of the AWS SDK's `GetSecretValueOutput` object from the [AWS SDK for Go](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/secretsmanager#GetSecretValueOutput)
233	
234	### Examples
235	
236	Given your AWS account's Secret Manager has the following data:
237	
238	- `/foo/bar/password` - `super-secret`
239	- `mysecret` - `bar`
240	
241	```console
242	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo") }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+sm:///foo/bar/password
243	super-secret
244	
245	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo" "/foo/bar/password") }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+sm:
246	super-secret
247	
248	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo" "/bar/password") }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+sm:///foo/
249	super-secret
250	
251	$ echo '{{ (ds "foo") }}' | gomplate -d foo=aws+sm:mysecret
252	bar
253	```
254	
255	## Using `s3` datasources
256	
257	### URL Considerations
258	
259	The _scheme_, _authority_, _path_, and _query_ URL components are used by this datasource.
260	
261	- the _scheme_ must be `s3`
262	- the _authority_ component is used to specify the s3 bucket name
263	- the _path_ component is used to specify the path to the object. [Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
264	- the _query_ component can be used to provide parameters to configure the connection:
265	  - `region`: The AWS region for requests. Defaults to the value from the `AWS_REGION` or `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` environment variables, or the EC2 region if run in AWS EC2.
266	  - `endpoint`: The endpoint (`hostname`, `hostname:port`, or fully qualified URI). Useful for using a different S3-compatible object storage server. You can also set the `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
267	  - `s3ForcePathStyle`: A value of `true` forces use of the deprecated "path-style" access. This is necessary for some S3-compatible object storage servers.
268	  - `disableSSL`: A value of `true` disables SSL when sending requests. Use only for test scenarios!
269	  - `type`: can be used to [override the MIME type](#overriding-mime-types)
270	
271	#### URL Examples
272	
273	Here are a few examples to help explain `s3` URLs:
274	
275	- `s3://mybucket/config/file.json`
276	  - the bucket region will be inferred, and the blob `config/file.json` in the `mybucket` bucket will be located in Amazon S3.
277	- `s3://mybucket/`
278	  - The contents of the bucket `mybucket` will be listed into an array. Note that only the last portion of the path (the file name) will be listed.
279	- `s3://mybucket/config/file?region=eu-west-1`
280	  - same as the first example, except the bucket's region is overridden to `eu-west-1`
281	  - the lack of file extension means that file will be parsed according to the file's `Content-Type` metadata
282	- `s3://mybucket/config/file.json?endpoint=localhost:5432&disableSSL=true&s3ForcePathStyle=true`
283	  - this example is typical of a scenario where an S3-compatible server (such as [Minio][], [Zenko CloudServer][], or testing-focused servers such as [gofakes3][])
284	  - the endpoint is overridden to be a server running on localhost
285	  - encryption is disabled since the endpoint is local
286	  - "path-style" access is used - this is typical for local servers, or scenarios where modifying DNS is impossible or impractical
287	
288	### Output
289	
290	The output will be the object contents, parsed based on the discovered [MIME type](#mime-types).
291	
292	### Examples
293	
294	Given the S3 bucket named `my-bucket` has the following objects:
295	
296	- `foo/bar.json` - `{"hello": "world"}`
297	- `foo/baz.txt` - `hello world`
298	
299	```console
300	$ gomplate -c foo=s3://my-bucket/foo/bar.json -i 'Hello {{ .foo.hello }}'
301	Hello world
302	
303	$ gomplate -c foo=s3://my-bucket/foo/ -i 'my-bucket/foo contains:{{ range .foo }}{{ print "\n" . }}{{ end }}'
304	my-bucket/foo contains:
305	bar.json
306	baz.txt
307	
308	$ gomplate -c foo=s3://my-bucket/foo/bar.json?region=eu-west-1 -i 'Hello {{ .foo.hello }}'
309	Hello world
310	
311	$ gomplate -c foo=s3://my-bucket/foo/bar.json?region=eu-west-1&
312	endpoint=my-test-site& -i 'Hello {{ .foo.hello }}'
313	Hello world
314	
315	$ gomplate -d bucket=s3://my-bucket/?region=eu-west-1&endpoint=my-test-site& -i 'Hello {{ (ds "bucket" "/foo/bar.json").hello }}'
316	Hello world
317	```
318	
319	## Using `consul` datasources
320	
321	Gomplate supports retrieving data from [HashiCorp Consul][]'s [KV Store](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/kv).
322	
323	### URL Considerations
324	
325	For `consul`, the _scheme_, _authority_, and _path_ components are used.
326	
327	- the _scheme_ URL component can be one of three values: `consul`, `consul+http`, and `consul+https`. The first two are equivalent, while the third instructs the client to connect to Consul over an encrypted HTTPS connection. Encryption can alternately be enabled by use of the `$CONSUL_HTTP_SSL` environment variable.
328	- the _authority_ is used to specify the server to connect to (e.g. `consul://localhost:8500`), but if not specified, the `$CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR` environment variable will be used.
329	- the _path_ can be provided to select a specific key, or a key prefix
330	
331	### Consul Environment Variables
332	
333	The following optional environment variables are understood by the Consul datasource:
334	
335	| name | usage |
336	|------|-------|
337	| `CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR` | Hostname and optional port for connecting to Consul. Defaults to `http://localhost:8500` |
338	| `CONSUL_TIMEOUT` | Timeout (in seconds) when communicating to Consul. Defaults to 10 seconds. |
339	| `CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN` | The Consul token to use when connecting to the server. |
340	| `CONSUL_HTTP_AUTH` | Should be specified as `<username>:<password>`. Used to authenticate to the server. |
341	| `CONSUL_HTTP_SSL` | Force HTTPS if set to `true` value. Disables if set to `false`. Any value acceptable to [`strconv.ParseBool`](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#ParseBool) can be provided. |
342	| `CONSUL_TLS_SERVER_NAME` | The server name to use as the SNI host when connecting to Consul via TLS. |
343	| `CONSUL_CACERT` | Path to CA file for verifying Consul server using TLS. |
344	| `CONSUL_CAPATH` | Path to directory of CA files for verifying Consul server using TLS. |
345	| `CONSUL_CLIENT_CERT` | Client certificate file for certificate authentication. If this is set, `$CONSUL_CLIENT_KEY` must also be set. |
346	| `CONSUL_CLIENT_KEY` | Client key file for certificate authentication. If this is set, `$CONSUL_CLIENT_CERT` must also be set. |
347	| `CONSUL_HTTP_SSL_VERIFY` | Set to `false` to disable Consul TLS certificate checking. Any value acceptable to [`strconv.ParseBool`](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv/#ParseBool) can be provided. <br/> _Recommended only for testing and development scenarios!_ |
348	| `CONSUL_VAULT_ROLE` | Set to the name of the role to use for authenticating to Consul with [Vault's Consul secret backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/consul). |
349	| `CONSUL_VAULT_MOUNT` | Used to override the mount-point when using Vault's Consul secret back-end for authentication. Defaults to `consul`. |
350	
351	### Authentication
352	
353	Instead of using a non-authenticated Consul connection, you can authenticate with these methods:
354	
355	- provide an [ACL Token](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/security/acl#tokens) in the `CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN` environment variable
356	- use HTTP Basic Auth by setting the `CONSUL_HTTP_AUTH` environment variable
357	- dynamically generate an ACL token with Vault. This requires Vault to be configured to use the [Consul secret backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/consul) and is enabled by passing the name of the role to use in the `CONSUL_VAULT_ROLE` environment variable.
358	
359	### Examples
360	
361	```console
362	$ gomplate -d consul=consul:// -i '{{(datasource "consul" "foo")}}'
363	value for foo key
364	
365	$ gomplate -d consul=consul+https://my-consul-server.com:8533/foo -i '{{(datasource "consul" "bar")}}'
366	value for foo/bar key
367	
368	$ gomplate -d consul=consul:///foo -i '{{(datasource "consul" "bar/baz")}}'
369	value for foo/bar/baz key
370	```
371	
372	## Using `env` datasources
373	
374	The `env` datasource type provides access to environment variables. This can be useful for rendering templates that would normally use a different sort of datasource, in test and development scenarios.
375	
376	No hierarchy or directory semantics are currently supported.
377	
378	**Note:** Variable names are _case-sensitive!_
379	
380	### URL Considerations
381	
382	The _scheme_ and either the _path_ or the _opaque_ part are used, and the _query_ component can be used to [override the MIME type](#overriding-mime-types).
383	
384	- the _scheme_ must be `env`
385	- one of the _path_ or _opaque_ component is required, and is interpreted as the environment variable's name. Leading `/` characters are stripped from the _path_.
386	
387	### Examples
388	
389	```console
390	$ gomplate -d user=env:USER -i 'Hello {{ include "user" }}!'
391	Hello hairyhenderson!
392	
393	$ gomplate -d homedir=env:///HOME -i '{{ file.IsDir (ds "homedir") }}'
394	true
395	
396	$ export foo='{"one":1, "two":2}'
397	$ gomplate -d foo=env:/foo?type=application/json -i '{{ (ds "foo").two }}'
398	2
399	```
400	
401	## Using `file` datasources
402	
403	The `file` datasource type provides access to files in any of the [supported formats](#mime-types). [Directory datasource](#directory-datasources) semantics are supported.
404	
405	### URL Considerations
406	
407	The _scheme_ and _path_ are used, and the _query_ component can be used to [override the MIME type](#overriding-mime-types).
408	
409	- the _scheme_ must be `file` for absolute URLs, but may be omitted to allow setting relative paths
410	- the _path_ component is required, and can be an absolute or relative path, and if the file being referenced is in the current working directory, the file's base name (without extension) is used as the datasource alias in absence of an explicit alias. [Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
411	
412	### Examples
413	
414	_`person.json`:_
415	```json
416	{
417	  "name": "Dave"
418	}
419	```
420	
421	_implicit alias:_
422	```console
423	$ gomplate -d person.json -i 'Hello {{ (datasource "person").name }}'
424	Hello Dave
425	```
426	
427	_explicit alias:_
428	```console
429	$ gomplate -d person=./person.json -i 'Hello {{ (datasource "person").name }}'
430	Hello Dave
431	
432	$ gomplate -d person=../path/to/person.json -i 'Hello {{ (datasource "person").name }}'
433	Hello Dave
434	
435	$ gomplate -d person=file:///tmp/person.json -i 'Hello {{ (datasource "person").name }}'
436	Hello Dave
437	```
438	
439	## Using `git` datasources
440	
441	The `git` datasource type provides access to files in any of the [supported formats](#mime-types) hosted in local or remote git repositories. [Directory datasource](#directory-datasources) semantics are supported.
442	
443	Remote repositories can be accessed by SSH, HTTP(S), and Git protocols.
444	
445	Note that this datasource accesses the git state, and so for local filesystem repositories, any files not committed to a branch (i.e. "dirty" or modified files) will not be visible.
446	
447	### URL Considerations
448	
449	The _scheme_, _authority_ (with _userinfo_), _path_, and _fragment_ are used, and the _query_ component can be used to [override the MIME type](#overriding-mime-types).
450	
451	- the _scheme_ may be one of these values:
452	  - `git`: uses the [classic Git protocol](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-on-the-Server-The-Protocols#_the_git_protocol) (as served by `git daemon`)
453	  - `git+file`: uses the local filesystem (repo can be bare or not)
454	  - `git+http`, `git+https`: uses the [Smart HTTP protocol](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-on-the-Server-The-Protocols#_the_http_protocols)
455	  - `git+ssh`: uses the [SSH protocol](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-on-the-Server-The-Protocols#_the_ssh_protocol)
456	- the _authority_ component points to the remote git server hostname (and optional port, if applicable). The _userinfo_ subcomponent can be used for authenticated datasources like `git+https` and `git+ssh`.
457	- the _path_ component is a composite of the path to the repository, and the path to the file or directory being referenced within. The `//` sequence (double forward-slash) is used to separate the repository from the path. If no `//` is present in the URL, the datasource will point to the root directory of the repository.
458	- the _fragment_ component can be used to specify which branch or tag to reference. By default, the repository's default branch will be chosen.
459	  - branches can be referenced by short name or by the long form. Valid fragments are `#main`, `#master`, `#develop`, `#refs/heads/mybranch`, etc...
460	  - tags must use the long form prefixed by `refs/tags/`, i.e. `#refs/tags/v1` for the `v1` tag
461	
462	### Authentication
463	
464	The `git` and `git+file` schemes are always unauthenticated, `git+http`/`git+https` can _optionally_ be authenticated, and `git+ssh` _must_ be authenticated.
465	
466	Authenticating with both HTTP and SSH requires the user to be set (like `git+ssh://user@example.com`), but the credentials vary otherwise.
467	
468	#### HTTP(S) Authentication
469	
470	Note that because HTTP connections are unencypted, and HTTP authentication is performed with headers, it is strongly recommended to _only_ use HTTPS (`git+https`) connections when accessing authenticated repositories.
471	
472	##### Basic Auth
473	
474	The most common form. The password can be specified as part of the URL, or provided through the `GIT_HTTP_PASSWORD` environment variable, or in a file referenced by the `GIT_HTTP_PASSWORD_FILE` environment variable.
475	
476	For authenticating with GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab and other popular git hosts, use this method with a _personal access token_, and the user set to `git`.
477	
478	##### Token Auth
479	
480	Some servers require the use of a bearer token. To use this method, a user is _not_ required, and the token must be set in the `GIT_HTTP_TOKEN` environment variable, or in a file referenced by the `GIT_HTTP_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable.
481	
482	#### SSH Authentication
483	
484	Only public key based authentication is supported for `git+ssh` connections. The key can be provided directly, or via the SSH Agent (or Pageant on Windows).
485	
486	To provide a key directly, set the `GIT_SSH_KEY` to the contents of the key, or point `GIT_SSH_KEY_FILE` to a file containing the key. Because the file may contain newline characters that may be difficult to provide in an environment variable, it can also be Base64-encoded.
487	
488	If neither `GIT_SSH_KEY` nor `GIT_SSH_KEY_FILE` are set, gomplate will attempt to use the SSH Agent.
489	
490	**Note:** password-protected SSH keys are currently not supported. If you have a password-protected key, use the SSH Agent.
491	
492	### Examples
493	
494	Accessing a file in a publicly-readable GitHub repository:
495	```console
496	$ gomplate -c doc=git+https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate//docs-src/content/functions/env.yml -i 'namespace is: {{ .doc.ns }}'
497	namespace is: env
498	```
499	
500	Accessing a file from a local repo (using arguments):
501	```console
502	$ gomplate -d which=git+file:///repos/go-which/ -i 'GOPATH on Windows is {{ (datasource "which" ".//appveyor.yml").environment.GOPATH }}'
503	GOPATH on Windows is c:\gopath
504	```
505	
506	Accessing a directory at a specific tag:
507	```console
508	$ gomplate -d 'cmd=git+https://github.com/hairyhenderson/go-which//cmd/which#refs/tags/v0.1.0' -i '{{ ds "cmd" }}'
509	[main.go]
510	```
511	
512	Authenticating with the SSH Agent
513	```console
514	$ gomplate -d 'which=git+ssh://git@github.com/hairyhenderson/go-which/' -i '{{ len (ds "which") }}'
515	18
516	```
517	
518	Using arguments to specify different repos
519	```console
520	$ gomplate -d 'hairyhenderson=git+https://github.com/hairyhenderson/' -i '{{ (ds "hairyhenderson" "gomplate//docs-src/content/functions/env.yml").ns }}'
521	env
522	```

524	## Using Google Cloud Storage (`gs`) datasources
525	
526	### URL Considerations
527	
528	The _scheme_, _authority_, _path_, and _query_ URL components are used by this datasource.
529	
530	- the _scheme_ must be `gs`
531	- the _authority_ component is used to specify the bucket name
532	- the _path_ component is used to specify the path to the object. [Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
533	- the _query_ component can be used to provide parameters to configure the connection:
534	  - `access_id`: (optional) Usually unnecessary. Sets the GoogleAccessID (see https://pkg.go.dev/cloud.google.com/go/storage#SignedURLOptions)
535	  - `private_key_path`: (optional) Usually unnecessary. Sets the path to the Google service account private key (see https://pkg.go.dev/cloud.google.com/go/storage#SignedURLOptions)
536	  - `type`: can be used to [override the MIME type](#overriding-mime-types)
537	
538	### Authentication
539	
540	All `gs` datasources need credentials, provided by the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` environment variable. This should point to an authentication configuration JSON file.
541	
542	See Google Cloud's [Getting Started with Authentication](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/getting-started) documentation for details.
543	
544	### Output
545	
546	The output will be the object contents, parsed based on the discovered [MIME type](#mime-types).
547	
548	### Examples
549	
550	Given the bucket named `my-bucket` has the following objects:
551	
552	- `foo/bar.json` - `{"hello": "world"}`
553	- `foo/baz.txt` - `hello world`
554	
555	```console
556	$ gomplate -c foo=gs://my-bucket/foo/bar.json -i 'Hello {{ .foo.hello }}'
557	Hello world
558	
559	$ gomplate -c foo=gs://my-bucket/foo/ -i 'my-bucket/foo contains:{{ range .foo }}{{ print "\n" . }}{{ end }}'
560	my-bucket/foo contains:
561	bar.json
562	baz.txt
563	```
564	
565	## Using `gcp+meta` datasources
566	
567	The `gcp+meta://` scheme provides access to the [GCP VM Metadata Service][], which is available to Google Cloud Platform VM instances. This service provides information about the instance, project, and custom metadata.
568	
569	This datasource can be used as an alternative to the [`gcp.Meta`][] function, and provides [directory](#directory-datasources) semantics for exploring metadata hierarchies.
570	
571	**Note:** This datasource is only functional when running on a GCP Compute Engine VM (or in an environment where the metadata service is available, such as Cloud Run or GKE).
572	
573	### URL Considerations
574	
575	The _scheme_ and _path_ URL components are used by this datasource.
576	
577	- the _scheme_ must be `gcp+meta`
578	- the _path_ component is used to specify the root of the metadata hierarchy. The two main categories are:
579	  - `/instance`: instance metadata specific to the VM (e.g., id, hostname, zone, network-interfaces)
580	  - `/project`: project metadata shared across all VMs in the project (e.g., project-id, attributes)
581	
582	[Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
583	
584	### Environment Variables
585	
586	The following optional environment variables are understood by the `gcp+meta` datasource:
587	
588	| name | usage |
589	|------|-------|
590	| `GCP_META_ENDPOINT` | _(Default `http://metadata.google.internal`)_ Sets the base address of the instance metadata service. Useful for testing or in non-standard environments. |
591	
592	### Examples
593	
594	Reading instance metadata:
595	
596	```console
597	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'The instance ID is: {{ include "meta" "instance/id" }}'
598	The instance ID is: 1234567890123456789
599	
600	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'The hostname is: {{ include "meta" "instance/hostname" }}'
601	The hostname is: my-instance.c.my-project.internal
602	
603	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'The zone is: {{ include "meta" "instance/zone" }}'
604	The zone is: projects/1234567890/zones/us-central1-a
605	```
606	
607	Reading project metadata:
608	
609	```console
610	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'The project ID is: {{ include "meta" "project/project-id" }}'
611	The project ID is: my-gcp-project
612	
613	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'Project numeric ID: {{ include "meta" "project/numeric-project-id" }}'
614	Project numeric ID: 1234567890
615	```
616	
617	Reading custom project attributes:
618	
619	```console
620	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'My attribute: {{ include "meta" "project/attributes/my-custom-attribute" }}'
621	My attribute: some-value
622	```
623	
624	Using directory semantics to explore available metadata:
625	
626	```console
627	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i '{{ ds "meta" }}'
628	[instance project]
629	
630	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:///instance/ -i '{{ ds "meta" }}'
631	[attributes cpu-platform description disks hostname id ...]
632	```
633	
634	Reading network interface information:
635	
636	```console
637	$ gomplate -d meta=gcp+meta:/// -i 'IP: {{ include "meta" "instance/network-interfaces/0/ip" }}'
638	IP: 10.128.0.2
639	```
640	
641	## Using `http` datasources
642	
643	To access datasources from HTTP sites or APIs, simply use a `http` or `https` URL:
644	
645	```console
646	$ gomplate -d foo=https://httpbin.org/get -i 'Hello there, {{ (ds "foo").headers.Host }}...'
647	Hello there, httpbin.org...
648	$ gomplate -d foo=https://httpbin.org/get -i '{{ $d := ds "foo" }}Hello there, {{ $d.headers.Host }}, you are looking very {{ index $d.headers "User-Agent" }} today...'
649	Hello there, httpbin.org, you are looking very Go-http-client/1.1 today...
650	```
651	
652	### Sending HTTP headers
653	
654	Additional headers can be provided with the `--datasource-header`/`-H` option:
655	
656	```console
657	$ gomplate -d foo=https://httpbin.org/get -H 'foo=Foo: bar' -i '{{(datasource "foo").headers.Foo}}'
658	bar
659	```
660	
661	This can be useful for providing API tokens to authenticated HTTP-based APIs.
662	
663	## Using `merge` datasources
664	
665	The `merge` scheme can be used to merge two or more other datasources together.
666	
667	`merge:` uses an [_opaque_ URI](#opaque-uris) format, where the _path_ component
668	is a list of datasource aliases or URLs, separated by the `|` character. The
669	datasources are read and merged together from right to left (i.e. the left-most
670	datasource values _override_ those to the right).
671	
672	Multiple different formats can be mixed, as long as they produce maps with string
673	keys as their data type.
674	
675	The [`coll.Merge`][] function is used to perform the merge operation.
676	
677	### Merging separately-defined datasources
678	
679	Consider this example:
680	
681	```console
682	$ gomplate -d "foo=merge:foo|bar|baz" -d foo=... -d bar=... -d baz=... ...
683	```
684	
685	This will read the `foo`, `bar`, and `baz` datasources (which must be otherwise
686	defined), and then overlay `bar`'s values on top of `baz`'s, then `foo`'s values
687	on top of those.
688	
689	The disadvantage with this option is verbosity, but the advantage is that the
690	individual datasources can still be referenced.
691	
692	### Merging datasources defined in-line
693	
694	Here's an example using URLs instead of aliases:
695	
696	```console
697	$ gomplate -d "foo=merge:./config/main.yaml|http://example.com/defaults.json" ...
698	```
699	
700	This has the advantage of being slightly less verbose. Note that relative URLs
701	in a subdirectory are supported in this context, as well as any other supported
702	datasource URL.
703	
704	A caveat to defining datasources in-line is that the _query_ and _fragment_
705	components of the URI are interpreted as part of the `merge:` URI. To merge
706	datasources with query strings or fragments, define separate sources first and
707	use the aliases. Similarly, extra HTTP headers can only be defined for separately-
708	defined datasources.
709	
710	## Using `stdin` datasources
711	
712	Normally _Stdin_ is used as the input for the template, but it can also be used
713	to stream a datasource. To do this, specify a URL with the `stdin:` scheme.
714	
715	In order for structured input to be correctly parsed, the URL can be given a "fake" file name with a supported extension, or the [MIME type can be explicitly set](#overriding-mime-types). If the input is unstructured (i.e. if the data is being included verbatim with the [`include`][] function), the scheme alone is enough.
716	
717	```console
718	$ echo 'foo: bar' | gomplate -i '{{(ds "data").foo}}' -d data=stdin:///foo.yaml
719	bar
720	$ echo 'foo' | gomplate -i '{{ include "data" }}' -d data=stdin:
721	foo
722	$ echo '["one", "two"]' | gomplate -i '{{index (ds "data") 1 }}' -d data=stdin:?type=application/array%2Bjson
723	two
724	```
725	
726	## Using `vault` datasources
727	
728	Gomplate can retrieve secrets and other data from [HashiCorp Vault][].
729	
730	### URL Considerations
731	
732	The _scheme_, _authority_, _path_, and _query_ URL components are used by this datasource.
733	
734	- the _scheme_ must be one of `vault`, `vault+https` (same as `vault`), or `vault+http`. The latter can be used to access [dev mode](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/dev-server) Vault servers, for test purposes. Otherwise, all connections to Vault are encrypted with TLS.
735	- the _authority_ component can optionally be used to specify the Vault server's hostname and port. This overrides the value of `$VAULT_ADDR`.
736	- the _path_ component can optionally be used to specify a full or partial path to a secret. The second argument to the [`datasource`][] function is appended to provide the full secret path. [Directory](#directory-datasources) semantics are available when the path ends with a `/` character.
737	- the _query_ component is used to provide parameters to dynamic secret back-ends that require these. The values are included in the JSON body of the `POST` request. The `version` parameter in particular can be used to specify the version of a secret when using the KV v2 secrets engine.
738	
739	These are all valid `vault` URLs:
740	
741	- `vault:`, `vault://`, `vault:///` - these all require the [`datasource`][] function to provide the secret path
742	- `vault://vault.example.com:8200` - connect to `vault.example.com` over HTTPS at port `8200`. The path will be provided by [`datasource`][]
743	- `vault:///ssh/creds/foo?ip=10.1.2.3&username=user` - create a dynamic secret with the parameters `ip` and `username` provided in the body
744	- `vault:///secret/configs/` - returns a list of key names with the prefix of `secret/configs/`
745	
746	### KV secrets engine - version 2 support
747	
748	Vault's KV secrets engine version 2 is supported automatically. In order to access specific versions of secrets, you may provide the `version` query parameter.
749	
750	### Vault Authentication
751	
752	This table describes the currently-supported authentication mechanisms and how to use them, in order of precedence:
753	
754	| auth back-end | configuration |
755	|-------------:|---------------|
756	| [`approle`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/approle) | Environment variables `$VAULT_ROLE_ID` and `$VAULT_SECRET_ID` must be set to the appropriate values.<br/> If the back-end is mounted to a different location, set `$VAULT_AUTH_APPROLE_MOUNT`. |
757	| [`github`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/github) | Environment variable `$VAULT_AUTH_GITHUB_TOKEN` must be set to an appropriate value.<br/> If the back-end is mounted to a different location, set `$VAULT_AUTH_GITHUB_MOUNT`. |
758	| [`userpass`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/userpass) | Environment variables `$VAULT_AUTH_USERNAME` and `$VAULT_AUTH_PASSWORD` must be set to the appropriate values.<br/> If the back-end is mounted to a different location, set `$VAULT_AUTH_USERPASS_MOUNT`. |
759	| [`token`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/token) | Determined from either the `$VAULT_TOKEN` environment variable, or read from the file `~/.vault-token` |
760	| [`aws`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/aws) | The env var  `$VAULT_AUTH_AWS_ROLE` defines the [role](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/aws#role-4) to log in with - defaults to the AMI ID of the EC2 instance. Usually a [Client Nonce](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/auth/aws#client-nonce) should be used as well. Set `$VAULT_AUTH_AWS_NONCE` to the nonce value. The nonce can be generated and stored by setting `$VAULT_AUTH_AWS_NONCE_OUTPUT` to a path on the local filesystem.<br/>If the back-end is mounted to a different location, set `$VAULT_AUTH_AWS_MOUNT`.|
761	
762	_**Note:**_ The secret values listed in the above table can either be set in environment variables or provided in files. This can increase security when using [Docker Swarm Secrets](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/secrets/), for example. To use files, specify the filename by appending `_FILE` to the environment variable, (i.e. `VAULT_USER_ID_FILE`). If the non-file variable is set, this will override any `_FILE` variable and the secret file will be ignored.
763	
764	### Vault Permissions
765	
766	The correct capabilities must be allowed for the [authenticated](#vault-authentication) credentials. See the [Vault documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/concepts/policies#capabilities) for full details.
767	
768	- regular secret read operations require the `read` capability
769	- dynamic secret generation requires the `create` and `update` capabilities
770	- list support requires the `list` capability
771	
772	### Vault Environment variables
773	
774	In addition to the variables documented [above](#vault-authentication), a number of environment variables are interpreted by the Vault client, and are documented in the [official Vault documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands#configure-environment-variables).
775	
776	### Examples
777	
778	```console
779	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:///secret/sneakers -i 'My voice is my passport. {{(datasource "vault").value}}' 
780	My voice is my passport. Verify me.
781	```
782	
783	For KV v2 secrets engine, specifying a version:
784	
785	```console
786	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:///kv2/sneakers?version=2 -i 'My voice is my passport. {{(datasource "vault").data.value}}'
787	My voice is my passport. Verify me.
788	```
789	
790	You can also specify the secret path in the template by omitting the path portion of the URL:
791	
792	```console
793	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:/// -i 'My voice is my passport. {{(datasource "vault" "secret/sneakers").value}}'
794	My voice is my passport. Verify me.
795	```
796	
797	And the two can be mixed to scope secrets to a specific namespace:
798	
799	```console
800	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:///secret/production -i 'db_password={{(datasource "vault" "db/pass").value}}' 
801	db_password=prodsecret
802	```
803	
804	If you are unable to set the `VAULT_ADDR` environment variable, or need to
805	specify multiple Vault datasources connecting to different servers, you can set
806	the address as part of the URL:
807	
808	```console
809	$ gomplate -d v=vault://vaultserver.com/secret/foo -i '{{ (ds "v").value }}'
810	bar
811	```
812	
813	To use dynamic secrets:
814	
815	```console
816	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:/// -i 'otp={{(ds "vault" "ssh/creds/test?ip=10.1.2.3&username=user").key}}'
817	otp=604a4bd5-7afd-30a2-d2d8-80c4aebc6183
818	```
819	
820	With the AWS auth back-end:
821	
822	```console
823	$ export VAULT_AUTH_AWS_NONCE_FILE=/tmp/vault-aws-nonce
824	$ export VAULT_AUTH_AWS_NONCE_OUTPUT=$VAULT_AUTH_AWS_NONCE_FILE
825	$ gomplate -d vault=vault:///secret/foo -i '{{ (ds "vault").value }}'
826	...
827	```
828	
829	The file `/tmp/vault-aws-nonce` will be created if it didn't already exist, and further executions of `gomplate` can re-authenticate securely.

105	Produces:
106	
107	```
108	Hello, Foo!Hello,  bar!Hello,  baz!
109	```
110	
111	## Variables
112	
113	The result of an action can be assigned to a _variable_, which is denoted by a
114	leading `$` character, followed by an alphanumeric string. For example:
115	
116	```
117	{{ $w := "world" }}
118	Hello, {{ print $w }}!
119	Goodbye, {{ print $w }}.
120	```
121	
122	this will render as:
123	
124	```
125	Hello, world!
126	Goodbye, world.
127	```
128	
129	Variables are declared with `:=`, and can be redefined with `=`:
130	
131	```
132	{{ $w := "hello" }}
133	{{ $w = "goodbye" }}
134	```
135	
136	### Variable scope
137	
138	A variable's scope extends to the `end` action of the control structure (`if`,
139	`with`, or `range`) in which it is declared, or to the end of the template if
140	there is no such control structure.
141	
142	In other words, if a variable is initialized inside an `if` or `else` block,
143	it cannot be referenced outside that block.
144	
145	This template will error with `undefined variable "$w"` since `$w` is only
146	declared within `if`/`else` blocks:
147	
148	```
149	{{ if 1 }}
150	{{ $w := "world" }}
151	{{ else }}
152	{{ $w := "earth" }}
153	{{ end }}
154	
155	Hello, {{ print $w }}!
156	Goodbye, {{ print $w }}.
157	```
158	
159	One way to approach this is to declare the variable first to an empty value:
160	
161	```
162	{{ $w := "" }}
163	{{ if 1 }}
164	{{ $w = "world" }}
165	{{ else }}
166	{{ $w = "earth" }}
167	{{ end -}}
168	
169	Hello, {{ print $w }}!
170	Goodbye, {{ print $w }}.
171	```
172	
173	## Indexing arrays and maps
174	
175	Occasionally, multi-dimensional data such as arrays (lists, slices) and maps
176	(dictionaries) are used in templates, sometimes through the use of
177	[data sources][]. Accessing values within these data can be done in a few ways
178	which bear clarifying.
179	
180	### Arrays
181	
182	Arrays are always numerically-indexed, and individual values can be accessed with the `index` built-in function:
183	
184	```
185	{{ index $array 0 }}
186	```
187	
188	To visit each value, you can loop through an array with `range`:
189	
190	```
191	{{ range $array }}
192	do something with {{ . }}...
193	{{ end }}
194	```
195	
196	If you need to keep track of the index number, you can declare two variables, separated by a comma:
197	
198	```
199	{{ range $index, $element := $array }}
200	do something with {{ $element }}, which is number {{ $index }}
201	{{ end }}
202	```
203	
204	### Maps
205	
206	For maps, accessing values can be done with the `.` operator. Given a map `$map`
207	with a key `foo`, you could access it like:
208	
209	```
210	{{ $map.foo }}
211	```
212	
213	However, this kind of access is limited to keys which are strings and contain
214	only characters in the set (`a`-`z`,`A`-`Z`,`_`,`1`-`9`), and which do not begin
215	with a number. If the key doesn't conform to these rules, you can use the `index`
216	built-in function instead:
217	
218	```
219	{{ index $map "foo-bar" }}
220	```
221	
222	`index` also supports nested keys and can be combined with other functions as such:
223	
224	```
225	{{ index $map "foo" (env.Getenv "BAR") "baz" ... }}
226	``` 
227	
228	**Note:** _while `index` can be used to access awkwardly-named values in maps,
229	it behaves differently than the `.` operator. If the key doesn't exist, `index`
230	will simply not return a value, while `.` will error._
231	
232	And, similar to arrays, you can loop through a map with the `range`:
233	
234	```
235	{{ range $map }}
236	The value is {{ . }}
237	{{ end }}
238	```
239	
240	Or if you need keys as well:
241	
242	```
243	{{ range $key, $value := $map }}
244	{{ $key }}'s value is: {{ $value }}
245	{{ end }}
246	```
247	
248	## Functions
249	
250	Almost all of gomplate's utility is provided as _functions._ These are key
251	words (like `print` in the previous examples) that perform some action.
252	
253	See the [functions documentation](/functions/) for more information.
254	
255	## The Context
256	
257	Go templates are always executed with a _context_. You can reference the context
258	with the `.` (period) character, and you can set the context in a block with the
259	`with` action. Like so:
260	
261	```
262	$ gomplate -i '{{ with "foo" }}The context is {{ . }}{{ end }}'
263	The context is foo
264	```
265	
266	Templates rendered by gomplate always have a _default_ context. You can populate
267	the default context from data sources with the [`--context`/`c`](../usage/#--context-c)
268	flag. The special context item [`.Env`](#env) is available for referencing the
269	system's environment variables _(unless overridden with `--context .=...` - see
270	[`env.Env`](../functions/env/#envenv) for an alternative)._
271	
272	_Note:_ The initial context (`.`) is always available as the variable `$`,
273	so the initial context is always available, even when shadowed with `range`
274	or `with` blocks:
275	
276	```
277	$ echo '{"bar":"baz"}' | gomplate -c .=stdin:///in.json -i 'context is: {{ . }}
278	{{ with "foo" }}now context is {{ . }}
279	but the original context is still {{ $ }}
280	{{ end }}'
281	context is: map[bar:baz]
282	now context is foo
283	but the original context is still map[bar:baz]
284	```
285	
286	## Nested templates
287	
288	Gomplate supports nested templates, using Go's `template` action. These can be
289	defined in-line with the `define` action, or external data can be used with the
290	[`--template`/`-t`](../usage/#--template-t) flag.
291	
292	Note that nested templates do _not_ have access to gomplate's default
293	[context](#the-context) (though it can be explicitly provided to the `template`
294	action).
295	
296	### In-line templates
297	
298	To define a nested template in-line, you can use the `define` action.
299	
300	```
301	{{ define "T1" -}}
302	Hello {{ . }}!
303	{{- end -}}
304	
305	{{ template "T1" "World" }}
306	{{ template "T1" }}
307	{{ template "T1" "everybody" }}
308	```
309	
310	This renders as:
311	
312	```
313	Hello World!
314	Hello <no value>!
315	Hello everybody!
316	```
317	
318	### External templates
319	
320	To define a nested template from an external source such as a file, use the
321	[`--template`/`-t`](../usage/#--template-t) flag.
322	
323	_hello.t:_
324	```
325	Hello {{ . }}!
326	```
327	
328	```
329	$ gomplate -t hello=hello.t -i '{{ template "hello" "World" }} {{ template "hello" .Env.USER }}'
330	Hello World! Hello hairyhenderson!
331	```
332	
333	## `.Env`
334	
335	_**Note:** Consider using [`env.Env`](../functions/env/#envenv) instead, which will continue to work even if the context is overridden (e.g. with `--context .=...`)._
336	
337	You can easily access environment variables with `.Env`, but there's a catch:
338	if you try to reference an environment variable that doesn't exist, parsing
339	will fail and `gomplate` will exit with an error condition.
340	
341	For example:
342	
343	```console
344	$ gomplate -i 'the user is {{ .Env.USER }}'
345	the user is hairyhenderson
346	$ gomplate -i 'this will fail: {{ .Env.BOGUS }}'
347	this will fail: template: <arg>:1:23: executing "<arg>" at <.Env.BOGUS>: map has no entry for key "BOGUS"
348	```
349	
350	Sometimes, this behaviour is desired; if the output is unusable without certain
351	strings, this is a sure way to know that variables are missing!
352	
353	If you want different behaviour, try [`getenv`](../functions/env/#envgetenv).
354	
355	[`text/template`]: https://pkg.go.dev/text/template/
356	[`base64.Encode`]: ../functions/base64#base64-encode
357	[data sources]: ../datasources/
